justifications.clinical.clinicalOutcomes: No outcome studies comparing BCG vs non-certified geriatric OT.
justifications.clinical.efficiency: AOTA BCG exam plus experience requirements; significant investment.
justifications.clinical.caseloadApplicability: Applicable to any geriatric OT caseload; SNF, home health, acute care, and geriatric outpatient.
justifications.clinical.reimbursement: No BCG billing premium; professional credential only; no payer impact.
justifications.clinical.marketDemand: Moderate employer demand in geriatric and SNF OT settings.
justifications.clinical.patientSatisfaction: Older adults value geriatric OT expertise.
justifications.business.cashPayViability: Gerontology OT services skew Medicare-funded, with some cash-pay potential in home modifications, aging-in-place consulting, and driving rehab.
justifications.business.pricingLeverage: AOTA board cert supports premium positioning in niche consulting work.
justifications.business.marketDifferentiation: Uncommon OT credential; clear professional differentiator.
justifications.business.ownerLeverage: Supports an aging-in-place or fall-prevention consultancy model staffed by other OTs.
justifications.business.efficiency: Portfolio-based process is meaningful work but reasonable cost.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyRecognition: AOTA board cert is a strong faculty credential in OT academia, analogous to ABPTS in PT.
justifications.academicClinical.scholarship: Portfolio process encourages scholarly products; BCG holders well represented in OT geriatrics literature.
justifications.academicClinical.teachingValue: Directly supports MOT/OTD geriatrics curricular content.
justifications.academicClinical.evidenceDepth: Built on solid OT and rehab gerontology evidence.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyDemand: Frequently preferred in OT faculty postings, especially geriatrics tracks.
justifications.academicClinical.efficiency: Portfolio path is reasonable relative to academic value.
